## E0015 and the other const checks never run on an anonymous constant (`[0; f(2)]`, `N` of a generic argument, an enum discriminant expression)

`fn main() { let _ = [0; f(2)]; }` with a non-const `fn f` reports nothing in blaze. rustc reports E0015 "cannot call non-const function `f` in constants" at `f(2)`. blaze's check `hir_ty_mir::mir::const_check::const_check(db, def: DefWithBodyId)` (crates/hir-ty-mir/src/mir/const_check.rs:367) and its caller in hir (crates/hir/src/diagnostics.rs:2937) only visit functions, consts and statics. An array length inside a body is an `AnonConstId` (`InferBodyId::AnonConstId`), so it is never const-checked. Code with a non-const call in an array length (or any anonymous constant) is accepted, against no-fallback and superset-of-rust. Fix: key `const_check` and `const_context` by `InferBodyId`, with the context of an anonymous constant (rustc: `ConstContext::Const { inline: false }`). Then have hir's body diagnostics (db lane, cc) const-check each anonymous constant of a body. Test: blaze-diagnostics tests::check::a_non_const_call_in_a_constant_is_refused (#1440).
